Image scanning is off by default. When a server owner enables it, uploaded images, animated GIFs and link-preview pictures are checked only for severe graphic real-world gore and explicit nudity (exposed genitals or female breasts). Image scanning is no longer experimental. It checks only for graphic gore and explicit nudity. We tested it on 446 independent Wikimedia Commons images, and none of the 372 harmless ones were flagged, including swimwear, costumes with fake blood, nosebleeds, sports and games.
Blood alone no longer counts as gore: minor injuries, treated wounds and costume makeup are left alone.
Animated GIFs and WebP images are now checked frame by frame, so a harmful frame hidden in the middle of an animation is caught.
Very large and very wide photos are now scanned instead of skipped.
Text moderation is no longer slowed down while images are being scanned.
